title: Prescriptions Compliance Manual: Days Supply of a Lost-or-Stolen Replacement
content:
The theft replacement days supply is the days supply of a Kestrel Prescriptions refill with the fill reason lost or stolen replacement, dispensed before the refill-eligible date because the patient's medication was lost or stolen.

## Section 1 — The fill replaced and the daily units

The fill replaced is the prescription's most recent refill, and the prescribed daily units are the prescription's written quantity divided by its written days supply.

## Section 2 — The days supply

The theft replacement days supply is the days the replaced refill still had to run, being its days supply dispensed less the calendar days from its dispensing date, as day 0, to today, never below zero. The units of the most recent corrected remake on the prescription, when it was dispensed on or after the replaced refill's dispensing date, are medication the patient holds, and they are taken off after dividing them by the prescribed daily units. The result is never below zero and is taken down to whole days.

## Worked example (hypothetical: written 60 units for 30 days, so 2 daily units)

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Replaced refill | 30 days supply, dispensed on day 0 |
| Today | day 8 |
| Days still to run | 30 less 8: 22 |
| Most recent corrected remake | 10 units, dispensed on day 3 (on or after day 0) |
| Remake days | 10 divided by 2: 5 |
| Theft replacement days supply | 22 less 5: 17 |

## Other cases (hypothetical)

- The most recent corrected remake was dispensed before the replaced refill's dispensing date: it is not taken off, and the days supply is 22.
- A remake of 3 units: 1.5 remake days, 22 less 1.5 is 20.5, taken down to 20.
- A replaced refill of 30 days dispensed 35 days ago: never below zero, so 0 days still to run.
